_comment: Share of certified H-1B labour condition applications naming each prevailing-wage level, by fiscal year. THE TREND RUNS THE OTHER WAY FROM WHAT TWO YEARS IMPLIED: the Level I or II share FELL from 80.5% in FY2017 to 62.7% in FY2025, and Level I alone from 44.4% to 20.8%. Employers file higher on the scale than they did, not lower, and any page quoting the level figures must say so. The break is between FY2017 and FY2018 (Level I 44.4% to 17.9%); both files use the same column and visa-class field, so it is a real reading, and it coincides with the April 2017 executive order that put Level I filings under scrutiny -- a coincidence in time, not a demonstrated cause. THE LEVEL MIX IS A SEPARATE QUESTION from whether the wage clears a local median, which local_wage_comparison answers and where the picture is worse. PARTIAL YEARS ARE MARKED: a year assembled from fewer than four quarterly files is flagged complete_year false and must not be compared with a full one -- the level MIX is still meaningful for a partial year but the COUNT is not. Certified filings only, and VISA_CLASS matched exactly because 'H-1B1 Chile' contains 'H-1B'. SOME YEARS SHIP TWO OVERLAPPING ANNUAL FILES -- FY2018 has both an end-of-year release and a separate full-year one, and summing them doubled that year to 939,820 against a true 576,359. The larger is kept and the other recorded in superseded_duplicates. Column names and level spellings changed with the FLAG system in FY2020, and both forms are read. THIS IS WHAT WAS PROMISED, not paid, and filing at any level is lawful.
source: US DOL OFLC, H-1B LCA disclosure archive
